# Format fixture provenance

All text and raster artwork in this directory were generated for BusyBooks and
are dedicated to the public domain under CC0-1.0. They contain no third-party
book content. `../FONT-LICENSE` covers the embedded Noto Serif font in EPUB
fixtures; each corresponding EPUB also includes that license. No authoring tool
or proprietary RAR compressor is redistributed with these books.

`tools/make_format_fixtures.py` creates the OPF 2/NCX, EPUB-contained DTBook,
DRM-free `.kepub.epub`, FB2 and CBZ fixtures. It uses Python 3.12/Pillow 10.2 and
the system NotoSerif-Regular.ttf for the optional embedded-font fixture. ZIP
timestamps are fixed. The EPUB 2 files contain a genuine OPF 2 manifest/spine,
NCX with nested navMap/pageList, guide and legacy cover metadata. They do not
retain an EPUB 3 navigation document or EPUB 3 manifest properties. The separate
cycle/missing variants intentionally violate fallback requirements. Unit tests
validate this structure. `check_epub2_fixtures.py` independently checks the XML
trees against the official EPUB 2 Relax NG/DTD schemas in EPUBCheck 5.4.0
(44 checks for eight fixtures). The UTF-16 XHTML fixture records EPUBCheck's
UTF-8-only HTML lint; the stylesheet-only XML island records its missing-fallback
lint. Both constructions are permitted by OPS/OPF 2.0.1 and independently pass
the schemas. Deprecated MIME aliases produce expected warnings. See the exact
exceptions and normative links in `docs/development/format-verification.md`.
The two KEPUB samples add Kobo-style spans to DRM-free EPUB 2 and EPUB 3 controls;
they are EPUB compatibility fixtures, without account integration or a separate
renderer. DTBook uses the 2005-2 vocabulary; the UTF-16 fixture covers both byte
orders. The styled XML island retains its authored namespace/DTD and supplies
only a manifest `fallback-style` stylesheet. MIME aliases remain EPUB-contained.
`epub2-raster-fallback.epub` adds a real PDF and PNG before the original XHTML
in a spine fallback chain. NCX/page references target the original PDF spine
identity; the guide directly names a content document. The XHTML also embeds
the intermediate PNG, distinguishing content and resource resolution. This
fixture passes EPUBCheck without errors or warnings.

FB2 fixtures exercise UTF-8, UTF-16 and declared Windows-1251 with identical
content; raw XML and both eligible ZIP suffixes; ordered authors, series and
cover; nested sections, poems, citations, tables, images, additional note bodies
and backlinks. `fiction-idless.fb2` has an unnamed outer section and two unnamed
nested sections, plus an authored ID that collides with a generated candidate.
Invalid fixtures cover malformed XML, the wrong namespace,
unsupported encoding, ambiguous wrappers and empty wrappers.

Comic fixtures contain numbered/nested, Unicode and case-distinct paths, JPEG,
PNG and WebP, an EXIF-oriented image, mixed dimensions and ComicInfo RTL/spread/
cover/bookmark metadata. `comic-codecs.cbz` contains baseline/progressive JPEG,
RGB/RGBA/grayscale PNG and lossy/lossless WebP. The long fixture has 120 pages.
Corrupt image, CRC, duplicate/unsafe path, excessive dimensions, unsupported TIFF
and animated PNG variants are intentional rejection fixtures.

The six RAR4/RAR5 stored/compressed/solid fixtures and encrypted/multipart
rejection fixtures were authored with the official RAR 6.24 Linux x64 tool from
`https://www.rarlab.com/rar/rarlinux-x64-624.tar.gz`. RAR 6.x is needed to write
both generations. Set `BUSYBOOKS_FIXTURE_RAR` to that development-only tool when
running the generator. Encrypted fixture password: `fixture`. `qualify_rar.py`
also mutates headers/data in disposable copies to test CRC, unsafe/duplicate
names and ambiguous legacy RAR4 codepages; those mutations are not extra books.

`comic-cancellable.cbr` is generated by `tools/make_resource_fixtures.py` with
`--cancellable test/fixtures/formats/comic-cancellable.cbr`: RAR5 solid, one small
PNG and 64 eight-MiB repeated-byte resources. It demonstrates killing an active
decoder while output is being produced. The same script's `--large /tmp/large.cbz`
creates a 290,794,372-byte, 42-page stored CBZ from deterministic RGB noise. This
large fixture is deliberately generated outside the checkout and not shipped.

`SHA256SUMS` records the exact checked-in fixture bytes. Regeneration across
Pillow/font/authoring-tool versions can change encodings; update the checksums
only after repeating the corresponding qualification and rendering checks.
